answer: A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. The canyon multiplier is published, charged in ivory, and quartz lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 4 for each account already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 4634 identities would post 2891 proofs and burn roughly 44 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
